pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.claim: A cheaper compaction call — summarise incrementally from the prior state rather than re-reading the window
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.unit: bytes of the SECOND summarizer request (15 messages, incremental)
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.why: V-C finding 1c: `transcriptMessages = toSummarize.slice(1)` is BY CONSTRUCTION the new segment — material the prior state has never seen. Clipping it to 900 characters a body destroyed the only read those messages ever get (a 901–2,400-char body lost up to 62.5% of its middle, permanently). `5671ef7` restored 2,400 characters per result for every compaction; the 900-char rendering survives only for a body an ADOPTED compaction already showed the summarizer in full, and edit-tool and patch-shaped bodies are exempt even then.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.netEffect: Lane C's net prompt saving is 0 bytes and its net correctness change is two closed holes.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.remeasuredOnTheInstalledBinary: 16,023 and 21,629 — see `installedRemeasurements[4]`. The withdrawal landed exactly on V-C's arithmetic reconstruction of the pre-lane number.

pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.claim: Trim the working-phase doctrine — make `# Built-in modes on request` opening-only
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.unit: bytes of the working-phase system prompt on Lane C's own rig
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.why: V-C finding 2b: `AgentLoop.interject()` folds mid-run steering into the SAME run and `turn` only resets per `run()`, so a mode ask lands on a `turn > 1` working-phase request with the routing gone. `5671ef7` reverted the phase gate (`keep: (c) => c.hasModeTools !== false`) and added `modes` as a just-in-time doctrine section instead: 739 B injected once per session, on runs that used to get it nowhere at all.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.sectionSizeDisagreement: The section is quoted as 739 B (Lane C's per-section table and F-C's manifest), 740 B (V-C's re-render) and the delta as 741 B by all three reports. Not reconciled; the three numbers are within rounding of one measurement of one string and nothing depends on which is right.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.remeasuredOnTheInstalledBinary: opening 22,059 B, working 19,001 B, phase-switch saving 3,058 B on the integration rig's own fixture (a different fixture from Lane C's, so the absolute numbers differ; the pinned value the test asserts, 3,058, is unmoved). See `installedRemeasurements[4]`.

pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.claim: Stand the gates down more often — a write that changed nothing does not re-arm them
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.unit: completions on the no-op-write script (script B); the control (script C, a write that DID change a file) stays at 7 with `gate:execution-evidence`
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.why: V-A finding #1/#1b: the excuse predicate was FALSE as stated — four excused writes did change the tree (an `apply_patch` move, a delete of an empty file, an add of an empty file, and a `multi_edit` no-op on a non-UTF-8 file whose bytes went `ff fe` → `ef bf bd ef bf bd`). `1625db1` trusts an empty diff only for `action === "updated"`, makes `multi_edit` decide by BYTES, and extends the answer from 2 of 4 write tools to 4 of 4. The 7 → 6 case still costs 6.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.boundaryOfTheClaim: The pre-change 7 is UNVERIFIABLE on this tree (V-A #5a): reproducing it needs `packages/` reverted. What is verified is the post-change side and the control's asymmetry.

pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.claim: Batch the citation with the check by construction
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.unit: turns refunded on the 3-criterion script; completions are 9 BOTH WAYS
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.why: The completion count does not move and Lane A says so itself: the script decides when the model cites, so the three bookkeeping completions are the script's, not the harness's. §5.2 says in advance that a fixed script can only show a change in what the HARNESS spends. What A2 changes is what those completions cost — three turns of the run's budget, given back through the same `TurnRefunds` cap every gate refund uses. V-A #2 proved the refund is bounded and un-farmable: four citation-only batches after one check earn 1 refund, three identical citations in one batch earn 1, and the alternating-pair run moved the ceiling 8 → 10, exactly the cap.
pinnedBeforeAfterByLane.correction: V-A #2a: a citation the ledger REFUSED was still refunded and written to the audit trail as carried forward. `1625db1` moved the refund and the log line after execution, and only when every planned call succeeded.

realDefectsFound.what: P3B I2 put an origin on every synthetic re-prompt and the persistence seam files those as `user_msg` rows carrying `harness`. NOTHING READ THE MARKER. A gate, a nudge and — after 730fd97 tagged `drainHarnessNotes` — every just-in-time doctrine note reached the three readers that mean "what the user said": `/rewind`'s turn list, session replay, and the permission check's trusted-intent corpus.
realDefectsFound.howItSurfaced: `tests/integration/engine-interject.test.ts`: a two-message conversation came back with 2 KB of house style sitting between the founder's words, filed as the founder's words.
realDefectsFound.whyItMatters: The trusted corpus is the one that matters beyond cosmetics — a harness note carries connector notes and teammate mail, which nobody typed.
